title: Boolean Logic - OR
concept: The || operator returns true when AT LEAST ONE condition is true.
why: Sometimes you need flexibility: 'Is it Saturday OR Sunday?' OR lets you check if ANY condition passes.
syntax_ref: condition1 || condition2  →  true if at least one is true
tips: `||` means 'or' — true if any condition is true
Think of `||` as a relaxed gatekeeper: 'one yes is enough'
OR is great for fallback conditions: 'discount OR sale OR clearance'
Short-circuit: if left side is true, right side is never checked
common_mistakes: Using a single `|` instead of `||` — single `|` is bitwise OR
Writing `or` instead of `||` — XIOM uses symbols
Expecting `false || false` to be true — OR needs at least ONE true
